s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Purulent discharge for 10 months
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI
Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Purulent discharge for 10 months
No history of trauma to the head
Otherwise healthy
No symptoms of fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Node measures 11 × 7 mm
MRI shows high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
CT shows opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses
Histopathology reveals mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge

shortlist.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: MRI and CT findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus

shortlist.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purulent discharge and chronic inflammation in an otherwise healthy patient

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic inflammation and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on histopathology

shortlist.label: Actinomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic suppurative infection with no history of trauma

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of a swelling on the right upper eyelid with purulent discharge, combined with imaging findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus, are consistent with a frontal sinus mucocele. The MRI and CT findings, including high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, and opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
rejected.why: The lack of symptoms related to the nasolacrimal duct, such as epiphora, and the location of the swelling on the upper eyelid, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: The patient's otherwise healthy status and the absence of symptoms such as fever or nasal discharge make this diagnosis less likely. Additionally, the histopathology findings do not support fungal infection.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The patient's lack of systemic symptoms, such as fever or headache, and the absence of other typical findings, such as nasal discharge or lung involvement, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Actinomycosis
rejected.why: The histopathology findings do not support actinomycosis, as there is no mention of sulfur granules or actinomyces organisms. Additionally, the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a frontal sinus mucocele.
